clue.text: After a liaison's end, woman's heartache

indicators.note: the woman's name is placed after the opening letters, so it follows them in the build
the end of the word liaison means only its final letter is taken

parts.note: Gina is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A lover is heartbroken once an affair finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartache' is taken literally: the answer is a chest pain caused by the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal reading: a condition producing pain from the heart, so an ache of the heart in the medical sense.

clue.text: Group's chiastic rhyme scheme

definitions.meaning: the Swedish pop band that won Eurovision with Waterloo
a crossed pattern where the outer lines rhyme together and the inner pair rhyme together

explanation.definitionFit: The band's name and the letters labelling an enclosed rhyme pattern are spelt the same.

clue.text: Rabbit seen twice somewhere in France

parts.note: to rabbit is British slang for chatter, as is to gas
the word rabbit is read a second time, now as the animal, an old word for which is cony

explanation.surface: A rabbit keeps turning up in one French spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' does double duty: first the verb (to talk on), then the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gascony is a historic region of south-west France.

clue.text: Drink to fortify for embellishment

parts.note: to neck is British slang for drinking quickly
to lace a drink is to fortify it with spirits

explanation.surface: Spiking a drink makes it fancier.
explanation.definitionFit: A piece of jewellery worn round the throat is an ornament or adornment.

clue.text: Person stealing beer wants second drink

indicators.note: wants here means lacks, so a letter is missing from the beer

parts.note: Pils is a pale lager beer, short for Pilsner
lager is a drink

explanation.surface: A beer thief is after a second pint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wants' looks like desire but means lacks: PILS loses its S.
explanation.definitionFit: A plunderer or looter is a person who takes goods by force.

clue.text: Mostly tinned pulp caterer put away

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all of the phrase is used, losing its final letter

parts.note: something tinned is in a can

indicators.note: to pulp is to mash up, so the letters of caterer are mashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A cook stores tinned mush away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' trims IN CAN to INCA; 'pulp' makes RCERATE from CATERER.
explanation.definitionFit: To put away can mean to lock someone up in prison, which is to imprison or jail them.

clue.text: False information by great German chemist

parts.note: a lie is false information
great means big

explanation.surface: A great German scientist spread falsehoods.
explanation.definitionFit: Justus von Liebig was a nineteenth-century German chemist, known for organic and agricultural chemistry.

clue.text: Motioning to leave EU? This is very revealing

indicators.note: the letters of EU are to leave, so they are taken out of the word

parts.note: motioning means gesturing

explanation.surface: Signalling a departure from the European Union is a real eye-opener.
explanation.walkthrough: The E and U are removed separately from GESTURING, a nod to Brexit.
explanation.definitionFit: A skimpy undergarment covering very little, so it shows a great deal of skin.

clue.text: Awful ruling blocked by leading revolutionary

indicators.note: blocked by means something sits inside the word, obstructing it

parts.note: regnant means reigning or ruling

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the word for leading is read backwards

parts.note: up means ahead or leading, as in a match

explanation.surface: A dreadful regime is blocked by a top rebel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' looks like a rebel but reverses UP to PU.
explanation.definitionFit: Something repulsive or offensive is dreadful, an informal sense of awful.

clue.text: Split from sexually open-minded faction

parts.note: bi is short for bisexual
a sect is a faction

explanation.surface: A liberal group splits off from a party faction.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut into two halves is to divide, as with a line or angle.

clue.text: Feature of some wines, eight swallowed in bar

indicators.note: one word is swallowed inside another, so it goes within it

parts.note: to stop is to bar
a rowing eight is a crew

explanation.surface: A wine bar where eight people knock back bottles.
explanation.definitionFit: Many cheaper wines are sealed with a twist-off cap rather than a cork.

clue.text: Tot learning it, one getting potty?

definitions.text: Tot learning it, one getting potty?

indicators.note: potty is British slang for crazy, so the letters go mad and are rearranged

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A toddler learns to use the potty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potty' does double duty: the child's toilet and a signal to rearrange the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes a small child being taught to use a potty instead of nappies.

clue.text: MC Hammer set to star without old lady

indicators.note: without is used in its old sense of outside, so the rearranged letters go round the mother
to hammer is to beat out of shape, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: ma is a mother, an old lady in slang

explanation.surface: The rapper MC Hammer is about to become a celebrity, minus his mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'MC Hammer' looks like the rapper's name, but MC is the definition and 'Hammer' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: MC stands for master of ceremonies, the person who announces speakers at a formal dinner.

clue.text: Great structure broadcaster's right to include in romp

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite broadcaster, plus the possessive S

indicators.note: the letter is included in the word, so it goes inside

parts.note: a caper is a romp or frolic

explanation.surface: A broadcaster has the rights to show a big romp.
explanation.definitionFit: A very tall building is a great construction rising high over a city.

clue.text: Poseur swots up about literary work

indicators.note: about means going around, so the reversed revising word surrounds the story
in a down clue up means reading from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: to swot is to cram for an exam
a tale is a literary work

explanation.surface: A show-off student revises a classic novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses CRAMS to SMARC, which then goes about TALE.
explanation.definitionFit: A know-all or show-off is someone posing as cleverer than they are.

clue.text: Mogul's capital of precious metal with Russia's banks

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver
the outer letters of Russia

explanation.surface: A Mughal ruler's capital fund held in silver and Russian banks.
explanation.definitionFit: Agra in northern India was the seat of the Mughal emperors, home to the Taj Mahal.

clue.text: Liking what a songwriter may do

definitions.meaning: a fondness or taste for something
read as two words: write a song

explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a fondness; split in two it says to write a song.

clue.text: Assist with half of letters?

indicators.note: half of means only the second four of eight letters are used

parts.note: the full set of letters is the alphabet

explanation.surface: Help with half of the post?
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' suggests mail, but means the whole alphabet, whose back half is used.
explanation.definitionFit: To aid or help, especially in wrongdoing, as in aiding and abetting.

clue.text: 20 lady's plump for a queen giving a twirl

parts.note: to plump for is to choose, or elect

indicators.note: a twirl turns round, so these letters are reversed

parts.note: R is short for regina, queen

explanation.surface: A sad woman chooses a queen who spins round.
explanation.walkthrough: 20 is TRAGIC, so the definition is 'tragic lady'; 'giving a twirl' turns A R into RA.
explanation.definitionFit: Electra is the heroine of Greek tragedies by Sophocles and Euripides.

clue.text: One like Napoleon artist gets to pose

indicators.note: the letters are made to pose, so they are arranged in a new way

explanation.surface: A painter gets Napoleon to sit for a portrait.
explanation.definitionFit: Napoleon was a brilliant military planner, the model of a campaign planner.

clue.text: Wow! Current ruler drops ecstasy

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: drops means lets fall, so the letter is removed

parts.note: an empress is a ruler
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: The present monarch gives up drugs, to general amazement.
explanation.definitionFit: To wow someone is to dazzle or make them admire you.

clue.text: Mail penned by jerk is depressing

indicators.note: penned means enclosed, so the paper sits inside the jerk

parts.note: a tic is a sudden jerk
the Daily Mail is a British newspaper, and a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper

explanation.surface: A tabloid written by an idiot is a downer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' looks like an insult but is a twitch; 'Mail' is the Daily Mail, a British tabloid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deeply sad or calamitous is distressing, and so depressing.

clue.text: Danger's kept for one key war yarn

indicators.note: kept means held inside, so the abbreviation is placed within the word for danger

parts.note: danger is a threat; the 's stands for has
eg is short for exempli gratia, for example, here for one
Esc is the escape key on a keyboard

explanation.surface: Danger lurks in a wartime story.
explanation.definitionFit: A 1963 film about a mass breakout from a German POW camp, a classic war story.

clue.text: M&S clothing very large for fashion star

indicators.note: clothing means dressing around, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: the abbreviation reduced to its two letters
OS is short for outsize, very large

explanation.surface: Marks & Spencer dresses a supermodel in plus sizes.
explanation.walkthrough: M&S is Marks & Spencer, a British high-street chain.
explanation.definitionFit: Kate Moss is a famous British supermodel.

clue.text: Sue's books, one with a scandalous ending

parts.note: lit is short for literature, books
I is the Roman numeral one
-gate is a suffix added to make names for scandals, after Watergate

explanation.surface: Sue's novels include one with a shocking ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sue' looks like a woman's name but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To sue someone is to take legal action against them in court.

clue.text: Like film-maker's second try to knock out western

indicators.note: knocking out removes the letter from the phrase

parts.note: a director's second attempt at a shot is take two

explanation.surface: A director keeps reshooting a western.
explanation.definitionFit: To start liking someone or something is to warm to them, an idiomatic phrase.

clue.text: Why outspoken opportunist's put before court

indicators.note: the opportunist is placed before the letter in the build

parts.note: a chancer is an opportunist; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: outspoken means spoken out, so the word is said and its sound kept

parts.note: the word why is pronounced exactly like the letter Y

explanation.surface: Why has a chancer been brought before a judge?
explanation.definitionFit: The Chancery Division is a branch of the English High Court.

clue.text: Way a family member shows inactivity

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
sis is short for sister

explanation.surface: A sibling is idle in a family way.
explanation.definitionFit: A state of equilibrium or no change is a standstill or lack of movement.
